provenance.what: Callgrind instruction counts of crates/expanse/benches/leaf_cap_cascaded.rs (workload core_leaf_cap_cascaded_instructions: 1,000,000 uniform random keys masked to 63 bits, lambda = N / 2^(63-48) = 30.52; 1,000,000 hit probes and 1,000,000 rejection-sampled miss probes per arm) at the shipped LEAF_CAP = 32 and at LEAF_CAP = 48 by build-time patch of crates/expanse/src/types.rs; deterministic exact integers, no interval (AGENTS.md section 8.4). The cap-48 cell is a control, not a shipped configuration.
provenance.host: x86_64 dev host — Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2697 v4 @ 2.30GHz, 72 threads, Linux 5.15.0-185-generic; inside a rust:1.98 container (rustc 1.98.0 (88d9e12ae 2026-08-18), valgrind-3.24.0, iai-callgrind-runner 0.16.1, --cache-sim=yes, --security-opt seccomp=unconfined)
provenance.instrument_note: Ir is published as cost, not verdict: docs/BENCHMARKING.md rule 16 decides random point lookups by wall clock and hardware counters with intervals; the wall-clock pair for this cell is docs/benchmarks/hot_comparison/scripts/leaf_cap_cascaded_wallclock.sh and has not been run (#715 scope item 3). Cache-simulation columns are Callgrind's simulated hierarchy, not the host's.
provenance.structure_note: At lambda = 30.52 under LEAF_CAP = 32 roughly 35% of the 32,768 two-byte expanses have cascaded into a bitmap branch of single-key immediates (the 2M @64 census at the same lambda counts 22,970 of 65,536 = 35.05%); under LEAF_CAP = 48 essentially all of them are still a packed linear leaf of up to 48 keys. The memory cells beside the Ir cells are the same generator, seed, N and width from density_sweep (mem_used() byte accounting).
provenance.generator: XorShift64(0x0DDB_1A5E_5EED_0001) masked to 63 bits (population); XorShift64(0x51ED_0FF5_C0FF_EE01) masked to 63 bits, rejected on membership (misses); Fisher-Yates under XorShift64(0x9E37_79B9) (hit probe order)
